requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the Rust outline profile meets `rust_item_selectors`, and the tests cover its cases. I found no gaps.

**Implementation** (`src/outline/rust.rs`)
- `KINDS` maps every required item kind to an outline node:
  - Named by the `name` field: `function_item`, `function_signature_item` (`fn`), `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `union_item`, `trait_item`, `mod_item`, `macro_definition` (`macro`), `const_item`, `static_item`, `type_item`, `associated_type` (`type`), and `extern_crate_declaration` (`extern-crate`).
  - Named by a custom rule: `impl_item` and `foreign_mod_item` (`extern`).
  - Anonymous: `use_declaration` and `macro_invocation`.
- Segments are syntactic ancestry within a single file. `mod[external]` is just a node, and nothing resolves modules across files.
- `impl_name` builds the name from the `type` field and the optional `trait` field. That gives `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`, and `impl<T> Trait for Wrapper<T>` becomes `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`. The shared selector code percent-encodes names, so `impl [u8; 4]` becomes `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`.
- `extern_name` uses the ABI string content, or `Rust` when there is no ABI.
- `use` declarations are `NameRule::Anonymous`. Macro invocations are anonymous nodes only in item position, through `item_macro` and `in_item_list`. Expression macros inside function bodies are not nodes, so they do not pollute the outline.
- The extra kinds `extern-crate`, `function_signature_item` and `associated_type` fit "other items" and the function and type-alias categories. The profile documents them, so nothing is left unspecified.
- Selector spelling is documented in `md/reference.md`. The "Outline profiles" table lists the grammar nodes and naming for each kind. The Rust selectors paragraph gives examples, covers anonymous `use@…` and `macro@…`, and states that modules are never resolved across files.
- All of the code that carries out the requirement is marked `{impl}`. The comment, attachment and hash helpers are marked for `outlines`, `outline_comments` or `structural_hash`, which are other requirements.

**Tests** (`src/outline/tests.rs`)
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` checks selectors and round-trip resolution for:
  - an inline mod, an external `mod x;`, a struct, an inherent impl, a trait impl, and an impl on `[u8; 4]` (percent-encoding);
  - trait methods and an associated type, `extern "C"` and a bare `extern`, nested functions, and duplicate names (`#1`, `#2`);
  - `macro_rules`, a union, an enum, a const, a static, a type alias, and `extern crate`.
  - It also checks that the empty selector resolves to the root, that an ambiguous `fn[repeated]` fails, and that a missing selector fails.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` checks that `use` declarations are anonymous `use@` segments with distinct hashes, alongside the same named cases.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` checks the anonymous `macro@<12 hex>` form at top level, in an impl and in a mod. It also checks the generic impl name `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`, and that macros inside function bodies are not nodes (7 selectors in total).
- Failure cases are covered, and `selector.rs` tests cover parsing and encoding.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
